steps.thought: I will list all available tests to understand the test suite and choose the cheapest and most informative initial tests.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power_on_selftest to quickly check all communication buses and subsystems at a very low cost.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed boot, CAN nodes, UART, and I2C devices, but failed to read the camera sensor ID, pointing to a camera hardware or connection issue.

hypotheses.rationale: Failure to read camera sensor ID during power-on selftest is commonly caused by a loose or damaged camera CSI ribbon cable.
Failure to read the camera sensor ID could alternatively indicate a dead camera sensor module.

steps.thought: I will run the camera_selftest to gather more specific telemetry on the camera CSI errors and frame rate, which will help distinguish between a ribbon cable fault and a dead sensor.
steps.observation: The camera_selftest failed with a zero frame rate and unreadable sensor ID, confirming a camera subsystem failure. This points to either a ribbon cable fault or a dead camera sensor module.

hypotheses.rationale: Inability to read sensor ID and zero frame rate commonly stems from a loose or damaged CSI ribbon cable.
An unreadable sensor ID and dead video output can also indicate a failed camera sensor module.

steps.thought: Checking remaining subsystems to ensure no other hidden faults exist.
steps.observation: Battery rest check passed with normal cell voltages and minimal imbalance. This leaves the camera subsystem as the sole failing area, with confirmed unreadable sensor ID and zero frame rate.

hypotheses.rationale: Camera selftest and power-on selftest show zero frame rate and completely unreadable sensor ID, which is most frequently caused by an unseated or damaged CSI ribbon cable.
Total lack of communication and zero frame rate could also indicate a dead camera sensor module, though ribbon cable faults are more common.

steps.thought: I will search the failure library for camera sensor ID read failures and zero frame rates to see if ribbon faults and dead sensors have distinguishable characteristics in other tests.

args.query: camera sensor ID read failed frame rate 0

matches.title: Camera self-test fails with CSI CRC errors
matches.symptom_summary: Camera sensor ID reads correctly but self test fails. Frame rate below 28 fps and many CSI CRC errors on the data lanes.
matches.root_cause: CSI ribbon cable creased or partially inserted in the connector.
matches.rework_notes: Reseat the ribbon; replace it if creased.

matches.title: Camera frame rate low, no CRC errors
matches.symptom_summary: Camera self test reports frame rate around 15 fps with zero CRC errors and sensor ID OK. Camera firmware version string does not match the release.
matches.root_cause: Camera module shipped with old firmware set to a low frame rate mode.
matches.rework_notes: Update camera firmware. Zero CRC errors separates it from a ribbon fault.

matches.title: Camera not detected, no frames
matches.symptom_summary: Power-on self test cannot read the camera sensor ID. Camera self test fails with zero fps and zero CRC errors, meaning no data arrives at all.
matches.root_cause: Dead image sensor on the camera module.

steps.observation: The unit exhibits a completely unresponsive camera with unreadable sensor ID and zero frame rate, ruling out firmware or CRC communication errors and pointing directly to either a disconnected ribbon cable or a dead camera sensor module.

hypotheses.rationale: A total lack of sensor communication (unreadable ID and zero frames with zero CRC errors) is classically caused by a loose or unseated CSI ribbon cable.
An internal hardware failure of the image sensor itself could also produce a complete lack of response and zero frame rate.
